_comment: Fixture to exercise the builder and the lint without Athena. Examplex and Rivalbet are invented, and so are the why-now figures (1 in 5, 1 in 10). The benchmark figures (1,296 of 133,000, 30%, 77%, $11.6K) are the result of one real test query on three unnamed casinos, 90 days to 15 Nov 2026, kept so the example reads like a real deck. Proxy mode: Examplex has no labelled on-chain trail, so the deck is built on three crypto casinos of its size. The review block records real reviewer runs on this fixture.

buyer.company: Examplex: a crypto casino, three years old, licensed offshore, most players in Latin America
buyer.tone: crypto-native but professional; wary of vendor hype; will forward to the CEO

slides.title: Your next VIPs already play *somewhere else*
slides.subtitle: What on-chain data shows about players at crypto casinos like yours.
slides.notes: Open with the question, not with us: how do you tell a VIP from a tourist on day one?

slides.headline: When a rival stumbles, *players look elsewhere*
slides.effect: In the two weeks after, *1 in 5* of its depositors funded another casino. In a normal fortnight it is 1 in 10.
slides.basis: Measured on-chain, 22 Oct to 4 Nov 2026, against the six weeks before.
slides.notes: Say what we measured. Do not say players left Rivalbet: a fifth funded another casino, most kept both. The window is open, nobody has won it.

slides.line: players deposit under $500 at one casino and *over $5,000 at others*.
slides.basis: 1,296 of 133,000 players at three crypto casinos of Examplex's size, last 90 days. Not Examplex's own players.
slides.notes: This is the hidden VIP. Pause here. Ask how their VIP team would find these players today.

slides.headline: What one casino *can't see* about its players

items.label: play at two or more casinos
of deposits from the top 1%
items.detail: A few players carry the revenue.

items.label: median deposits elsewhere per hidden VIP

slides.basis: 133,000 players at three crypto casinos of Examplex's size, last 90 days.
slides.notes: One line each. The middle card is the one a CRM lead repeats to their boss.

slides.headline: Two ways to *act on it*

enrich.title: Know every player on day one
enrich.line: We add what players do elsewhere to the profiles you already hold.

advertise.title: Reach proven players
advertise.line: Advertise to adults who already play at comparable casinos.

slides.notes: Lead with Enrich for a CRM buyer. 'Limits' matters: the same data supports safer-gambling checks. Mention Advertise in one sentence.

slides.headline: See this for *your own market* in 20 minutes
slides.ask: Book 20 minutes. Nothing needed from you.
slides.notes: One ask, and it costs them nothing. The user sample comes second, under an agreement, once they have seen their market.

points: Public on-chain deposits to labelled casino deposit addresses, 18 Aug to 15 Nov 2026. Aggregates only: no names, emails or account data.
Peer set: three crypto casinos of similar size, serving Latin America. Examplex's own players are not in this data.
A hidden VIP deposits under $500 at one casino and $5,000 or more at others in the same period.
Outliers are capped, and every figure covers at least 3 people.

claims.source: fixture: whynow_switchers baseline, six weeks before

review.takeaway: About 1 in 100 players at casinos like mine look small but deposit over $5,000 elsewhere, and this vendor says it can flag them at signup.
changes: Round 1 (scores 2,4,2,2,2,3): peers were crypto casinos shown to a fiat operator; kicker said 'your players' on peer data; hero had no base; the Rivalbet effect had no baseline; the ask needed the buyer's user data; vague regulation event. All fixed, and each is now a lint rule or a rule in the guides.

Round 2 (scores above): wording fixed after the review and not re-reviewed: 'spend' to 'deposits', 'licensed markets' to 'markets you serve', the why-now headline no longer says 'right now', 'limits' removed.
open_objections: If you can see what my players do at rivals, can rivals target my players? Is my company in your data?
How is a player matched at signup, what must I provide, and what share of my base would match?
'Aggregates only' on the method slide against per-player enrichment in the product: which is it?
The top-1% share is something I can already see in my own back office.
review._note: Kept as a real 'revise': lint_deck.py --final fails on this fixture on purpose. The open objections need approved answers from Addressable (see references/buyer-review.md, standing objections), not better wording.
